In detail

No barrio-specific safety incidents were found for Cortes (Huertas, Santa Ana, Congreso area) beyond generic listicles that describe the wider Centro district as Madrid's highest-crime district without breaking figures down by barrio. Specific searches turned up only minor nightlife-noise complaints rather than robbery, drug-market, or violence coverage. No particular safety concern found in the source review. Sources checked: Madridiario (noise complaints, Plaza de Santa Ana); Generic district-level ranking articles checked but gave no Cortes-specific detail; No barrio-specific incident coverage found.

Frequently asked questions

Is Cortes safe?

Cortes was reviewed at area level and no traveller-relevant safety concern was documented for it in the sources checked. Wandroz records that as no findings, not as a safety rating: an absence of reporting is not evidence that an area is safe. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Madrid publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Why does Cortes have no rating?

Because the review found nothing to rate it on. Areas with documented, sourced signals get a level; areas without them are shown as reviewed with no findings, so you can tell the difference between an area that was checked and came back clear of documented issues and one that was never looked at. Both are treated as inconclusive here rather than as reassurance.

Is Cortes a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Nothing documented argues against it, and nothing documented argues for it either. For a stay, weigh it against the rated areas on the Madrid map and check recent reviews for the specific street. You can search accommodation already scoped to this area using the Booking.com link on this page.
